payload.root_cause: In `camelCase` in src/text.js, line 41 uses the wrong character index when capitalizing words after the first: `return i === 0 ? lower : lower[1].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1);`. It uppercases the SECOND character (`lower[1]`) and leaves the first character lowercase, so the original first letter of each subsequent word is dropped and replaced by the capitalized second letter. For input 'hello big world': 'big' becomes 'I' + 'ig' = 'Iig' and 'world' becomes 'O' + 'orld' = 'Oorld', producing 'helloIigOorld' instead of 'helloBigWorld'. The fix must be `lower[0].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)`. (The same expression is also fragile: for a single-character word, `lower[1]` is undefined and `.toUpperCase()` would throw a TypeError.)

payload.rationale: The root cause is an off-by-one index error on line 41 of src/text.js: for every word after the first, camelCase capitalizes `lower[1]` (the second character) instead of `lower[0]` (the first character). This drops the original first letter of each non-initial word and replaces it with the capitalized second letter ('big' -> 'Iig', 'world' -> 'Oorld'), yielding 'helloIigOorld'. Changing the index from 1 to 0 restores the documented behavior 'helloBigWorld'. It also removes the latent TypeError for single-character words, since `lower[0]` is always defined for the non-empty words produced by the split/filter (whereas `lower[1].toUpperCase()` would throw on a 1-char word). No other lines are touched.
